raw.abstractText:
Background

Tibial transverse osteotomy (TTO) is a promising but limited surgical option for diabetic foot (DF). Berberine, a natural compound from Coptis chinensis, exhibits anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic effects relevant to metabolic diseases.

Objectives

This study aimed to evaluate whether adjunctive berberine enhances the therapeutic outcomes of TTO in DF patients and to explore its potential association with the platelet-derived growth factor-B (PDGF-B)/PDGF receptor-β (PDGFRβ) signaling pathway.

Methods

This was a prospective, single-center, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, blinded trial. Of 200 screened DF patients, 96 eligible participants (Wagner grade 2-4) scheduled for TTO were randomized 1:1 to receive either TTO plus local berberine injections (n=48) or TTO plus local saline placebo (n=48). An additional non-randomized diabetic reference group (n=10) and healthy control group (n=10) were included for exploratory cellular studies only. The primary outcome was the total effective rate of ulcer healing at 3 months. Secondary outcomes included changes in Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI), ulcer area, Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain score and serum inflammatory markers (hs-CRP, IL-6). Exploratory outcomes comprised serum VEGF, bFGF and PDGF-B levels, as well as fibroblast apoptosis in wound tissue.

Results

All 96 randomized participants completed the 3-month follow-up, with no dropouts. The berberine group demonstrated a significantly higher total effective rate than the surgery-alone group (87.5% vs. 68.8%; risk difference, 18.7%; 95% CI, 1.2% to 36.2%; P < 0.05). At 3 months, the berberine group also showed greater improvements in ABI (mean difference, 0.13; 95% CI, 0.08 to 0.18; P < 0.01) and ulcer healing rate (mean difference, 16.7%; 95% CI, 9.5% to 23.9%; P < 0.01), along with more significant reductions in hs-CRP and IL-6. Berberine treatment was associated with reduced fibroblast apoptosis in wound tissue (mean difference, -1.10%; 95% CI, -1.56% to -0.64%; P = 0.001) and lower protein expression of PDGF-B and PDGFRβ. No severe adverse events related to berberine injections were reported.

Conclusion

In DF patients undergoing TTO, adjunctive local berberine therapy significantly improves the total effective rate and promotes ulcer healing, with benefits associated with reduced inflammation and fibroblast apoptosis and downregulation of the PDGF-B/PDGFRβ pathway. These findings are correlative and require further mechanistic validation. Larger multi-center trials are needed to confirm efficacy and safety.

raw.abstractText: Understanding cellular diversity within a tissue is essential to elucidate how distinct cell populations cooperate to maintain homeostasis, regenerate, and respond to aging or disease. Unlike bulk methods that measure averaged gene expression, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables high-resolution profiling of the transcriptomes of individual cells, providing a powerful tool for analyzing cellular heterogeneity. However, its application in skeletal muscle remains limited to the mononucleated cellular fraction, as standard single-cell approaches cannot efficiently capture muscle fibers due to their large and multinucleated nature. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq), which profiles individual nuclei rather than intact cells, offers a more suitable and technically robust approach, enabling comprehensive characterization of the transcriptional landscape across the entire tissue. In this chapter, we present a workflow for the bioinformatic analysis of snRNA-seq data generated from mouse skeletal muscle using the 10x Genomics Chromium platform. The chapter focuses on computational processing using R software and the Seurat package, including quality control, normalization, dimensionality reduction, clustering, and cell-type annotation. By applying this pipeline, researchers can identify distinct muscle-resident cell populations and explore the complexity of skeletal muscle. The described framework also illustrates how to perform downstream analyses such as differential gene expression and cell-cell communication analysis.

Although commercial extraction kits offer standardized workflows and reduce the handling of harmful reagents, the manufacturer's protocols are insufficient for root samples with high levels of secondary metabolites. This protocol describes the optimization of DNA extraction from coffee (Coffea arabica L.) roots colonized by AMF, based on the use of the commercial ZymoBIOMICS™ Quick-DNA fecal/soil Microbe Kit, designed for the rapid and simple isolation of microbial DNA and host cells from fecal and soil samples, incorporating a pre-maceration and pre-digestion step with proteinase K and β-mercaptoethanol. This modification significantly improves yield, DNA integrity, and PCR amplification of Glomeromycota-specific ribosomal markers (SSU/18S).

raw.abstractText:
Background

Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is involved in colorectal cancer (CRC) pathogenesis. Curcumin (CUR) is widely used in the treatment of CRC. Polystyrene nanoparticles (PS-NPS) have a high specific affinity and have an inhibitory effect on cell proliferation. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to investigate the mechanism of inhibition of EMT in colorectal cancer mice by preparing curcumin polystyrene nanoparticles (CUR-PS-NPS).

Objective

This study aimed to construct CUR-PS-NPS and investigate their mechanism in inhibiting CRC EMT via the miR-186/PI3K/AKT/Twist axis.

Method

CUR-PS-NPS were prepared and characterized. In-vivo , CRC model mice (Balb/c, male) were divided into four groups: sham-operated control (PC), CRC model (CRC), low-dose CUR-PS-NPS (Cur-PS-NPS-L), and high-dose CUR-PS-NPS (Cur-PS-NPS-H). After intraperitoneal injection, tumor volume, EMT marker proteins and changes in miR-186 and the PI3K/AKT/Twist pathway were measured. In-vitro, human normal colonic epithelial cells (NCM460) were used to validate miR-186 interference and SW480 cells were co-transfected with a PI3K inhibitor to clarify the specific mechanism by which CUR-PS-NPS inhibit EMT.

Results

In CRC mice intervened with CUR-PS-NPS, the tumor volume was reduced by 50%, the expression of mir-186 was up-regulated by 2.5 times, the phosphorylation level of PI3K/AKT was decreased by 40%, the expression of Twist protein was down-regulated by 35% and the expression of the EMT marker E-cadherin was increased. The expressions of N-cadherin, Vimentin and Snail decreased significantly.

Conclusion

CUR-PS-NPS can effectively delay the EMT process of CRC by up-regulating mir-186, inhibiting the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway and the expression of Twist. This discovery provides a new strategy for targeted therapy based on nanocarriers and its application potential in clinical practice can be further explored in the future.

raw.abstractText: Δ9-Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) is the principal psychoactive cannabinoid in cannabis. Following consumption, it is metabolized in the liver to 11-hydroxy-Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol, and subsequently to 11-nor-9-carboxy-Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol, which are excreted in urine. The presence of THC and its metabolites in urine can serve as indicators of recent or past cannabis use. Here, a routine method for the simultaneous quantification of these three compounds is presented, using tandem enzymatic-alkaline hydrolysis, solid-phase extraction, and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). The procedure is optimized for operational efficiency and analytical sensitivity and is routinely applied to urine samples submitted for cannabinoid testing in clinical and forensic toxicology.

raw.abstractText: Tryptamines constitute a class of organic compounds structurally derived from tryptamine, a natural alkaloid found in plants, fungi, and the human body. This group encompasses biologically significant molecules such as serotonin and melatonin, as well as psychoactive compounds like DMT and psilocybin. Tryptamines are typically classified into simple tryptamines and ergolines, with further subclassifications based on structural modifications on the indole ring system. Their primary mechanism of action involves modulation of serotonergic receptors, especially the 5-HT2A, often resulting in psychedelic effects. While some tryptamines are naturally occurring, others are synthetically produced and increasingly encountered as new psychoactive substances. The study presents a rapid and robust LC-MS/MS method for the simultaneous detection and quantification of 37 tryptamines in human urine and plasma. The method employs a ThermoFisher UHPLC-LC-MS/MS system using a Hypersil GOLD C18 column and gradient elution, with MS^n acquisition in positive ESI mode. Analytical validation demonstrated high selectivity, sensitivity, and reproducibility. Sample preparation was performed through a combination of liquid-liquid and protein precipitation extraction procedures. The method successfully identified tryptamines using product ion spectra compared to a reference spectral library, with detection limits, recovery, and matrix effects systematically evaluated. This analytical approach provides a reliable tool for forensic and clinical toxicology, particularly in the context of the increasing interest in tryptamines for both recreational and therapeutic purposes.

raw.abstractText: Oligopeptide-modified poly(β-amino ester)s (OM-pBAEs) are polymer-based delivery systems that enable the encapsulation and intracellular transport of nucleic acids, including messenger RNA (mRNA) and mixtures of mRNA with DNA. OM-pBAEs form cationic nanoparticles (NPs) through electrostatic interactions with nucleic acids, protecting them from degradation and enhancing cellular uptake. Terminal oligopeptides composed of lysine, arginine, or histidine enhance polyplex stability, nucleic acid binding, and endosomal escape. This chapter describes a protocol for preparing OM-pBAE nanoparticles, including polymer synthesis, peptide modification, controlled mixing with nucleic acids to form polyplexes, precipitation in RNase-free water, stabilization with excipients, and optional freeze-drying for long-term storage. Nanoparticle formation occurs at a constant temperature of 25°C, with incubation to ensure reproducible self-assembly. Nanoparticles are characterized by using dynamic light scattering (DLS) to determine particle size, polydispersity, and surface charge, while nucleic acid encapsulation efficiency is assessed to evaluate loading capacity. This protocol provides a versatile, nonviral platform for efficient nucleic acid delivery, supporting applications such as gene-editing experiments.

raw.abstractText: Radiation-induced crosslinking enables the fabrication of protein-based hydrogels and nanogels with tunable physicochemical properties without requiring chemical crosslinkers. Here, we provide protocols for the preparation of protein-based hydrogels that mimic the in vivo extracellular matrix and protein-based nanogels designed for nanomedicine applications, including magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) contrast agents and drug delivery systems (DDS). The method is based on ionizing radiation of aqueous protein solutions, where hydroxyl radicals generated by water radiolysis react primarily with aromatic amino acid residues (tyrosine, phenylalanine, and histidine), inducing intermolecular crosslinking. The resulting hydrogels and nanogels retain biocompatibility and enzymatic degradability while preserving key cell-adhesive sequences. Bulk hydrogels allow precise control over stiffness and surface topography, whereas nanogels offer size control and support straightforward functionalization. Representative applications include culturing various cell types, such as epithelial, fibroblast, muscle, and stem cell types, on hydrogels with tunable mechanical and topographic cues, and functionalizing nanogels for imaging and therapeutic use. This chapter focuses on gelatin-based hydrogels and nanogels. Supplementary notes direct readers to related protocols for collagen hydrogels and peptide-based nanogels. Collectively, these methods provide a versatile platform for biomaterials and nanomedicine research.

raw.abstractText:
Background

Liver fibrosis is a chronic wound healing process of liver injury and gut-liver axis dysregulation has been recently identified as an important contributor to liver fibrosis progression. Quercetin has been reported to have anti-inflammatory activity and microbiota-modulating effects. However, the potential targets of quercetin remain unclear, as does the relationship between quercetin-associated targets and changes in the gut microbiota in liver fibrosis.

Objectives

The purpose of this study was to use network pharmacology to predict potential targets of quercetin associated with liver fibrosis and to explore changes in gut microbiota following treatment with quercetin using a CCl4-induced rat model.

Methods

Eighteen male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomized into CON group, MOD group and QR group (n = 6 per group). Liver fibrosis was induced by weekly subcutaneous injection of carbon tetrachloride (CCl4) for eight weeks. Oral gavage of quercetin (50 mg/kg/day) was performed in QR group. Histopathological changes were assessed by hematoxylin-eosin staining, Masson staining and Ishak scoring. Potential targets of quercetin were screened using network pharmacology, followed by protein-protein interaction (PPI) network construction and Gene Ontology (GO)/Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses. Cecal microbiota composition was determined by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Parametric or non-parametric tests were used accordingly, including one-way ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis test.

Results

Histopathology revealed significant liver injury and fibrosis in the MOD group relative to the CON group. The QR group showed lower Ishak fibrosis scores and milder histopathological features compared with the MOD group. Network pharmacology analysis identified UBC, UBE2I, RBX1, PSMB7 and UBA1 as hub targets, with KEGG pathways of interest including the TNF signaling pathway, p53 signaling pathway, Toll-like receptor signaling pathway and ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis. Alpha diversity of the cecal microbiota differed significantly among groups, whereas beta diversity did not. Relative abundance of Proteobacteria decreased and Firmicutes increased in the QR group relative to the MOD group. Taxa enrichment analysis identified enrichment of Muribaculaceae and Ligilactobacillus in the QR group.

Conclusion

Histopathology and microbiome analyses indicated that quercetin intervention was associated with altered liver histopathological features and shifts in gut microbiota composition in rats with CCl4-induced liver fibrosis. Network pharmacology predicted several hub targets and pathways potentially linked to these observations. As the present analyses are purely correlational and lack mechanistic validation at the molecular level, no causal relationships are implied between the predicted targets/pathways and the observed histological or microbiome changes. These findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and warrant further validation studies.

raw.abstractText:
Background

 Fibrotic liver is one of the serious pathophysiological consequences of chronic injury to the liver, may progress toward serious complications including cirrhosis and hepatic carcinoma.

Objectives

Panax notoginseng is used for both therapeutic and prophylactic purposes in TCM; it is a source of Dencichine, an active substance that has been proven to exhibit antifibrotic properties in hepatic fibrosis. The present study investigated how Dencichine treatment ameliorates liver fibrosis using an animal model and a cellular fibrosis model.

Methods

Randomly assigned, male C57BL/6J mice received 10% CCl4 for 15 consecutive weeks to induce hepatic fibrosis. Treatment with Dencichine was initiated from 7th week onward. To simulate in-vitro the presence of a fibrotic microenvironment, LX-2 cells were treated with PDGF-BB at a concentration of 20 ng/mL and incubated from one up to four days and then treated by various doses of Dencichine. Liver function was evaluated by measuring alanine aminotransferase (ALT), AST, HA and LN. Histopathology was evaluated by haematoxylin/eosin (HE), Masson's trichrome and Sirius red stains. Quantitative real-time PCR and western blot analyses were used to evaluate mRNA and protein expression levels, respectively. Wound-healing assays and transwell chamber experiments were used to assess cell migration; EdU proliferation detection and flow cytometry were performed to measure cell proliferation and cell cycle, respectively.

Results

 The most important results are a considerable reduction of serum concentrations of AST and ALT, HA and laminin in CCl4-treated mice decreased liver injury and ECM deposition. Furthermore, this compound downregulated the expression of cyclin D1 and cyclin E1 and blocked the activation of PI3K and AKT kinases in fibrotic liver cells.

Conclusion

These results indicate that Dencichine may slow the development of liver fibrosis by interfering with the PI3K-AKT signaling cascade, demonstrating significant anti-scarring properties.

raw.abstractText: Opioid consumption has remained a public health problem, contributing to a significant number of fatal overdoses. Both opioids and metabolites can be detected in bile specimens due to hepatic metabolism and enterohepatic circulation, offering higher concentrations and a wide detection window compared to blood samples. Thus, bile is a suitable specimen that can provide supplementary data for routine forensic toxicology cases. This chapter presents a sensitive and specific method for the qualitative confirmation of morphine, codeine, and 6-monoacetylmorphine, a heroin consumption marker, in bile samples. The proposed methodology involves a solid-phase extraction procedure and subsequent analysis by gas chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry.

raw.abstractText: This chapter describes a liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) method for the determination of drugs of abuse and their metabolites in human urine. The target analytes include 11-nor-9-carboxy-Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC-COOH), benzoylecgonine, 6-acetylmorphine, morphine, codeine, 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA), 3,4-methylenedioxyamphetamine (MDA), amphetamine, and methamphetamine. Sample preparation involves enzymatic hydrolysis with β-glucuronidase, followed by dilution with methanol and centrifugation, enabling direct analysis without derivatization. Chromatographic separation is achieved within 4 min, and detection is performed in multiple reaction monitoring mode with deuterated internal standards for reliable quantification. This simple and robust approach fulfills international requirements for confirmatory urine drug testing and can be readily implemented in forensic and workplace toxicology laboratories.

raw.abstractText: The identification and quantification of drugs of abuse in biological specimens remain a key objective in forensic toxicology. Oral fluid has become a valuable alternative matrix due to its simple, noninvasive collection, minimal risk of adulteration, and good correlation with recent drug use. This chapter presents a validated gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) method for the detection and quantification of multiple drugs of abuse and metabolites in oral fluid samples using the dried saliva spot (DSS) technique. The target analytes include amphetamine (ANF), methamphetamine (MANF), 3,4-methylenedioxyamphetamine (MDA), 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA), cocaine (COC), benzoylecgonine (BE), Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), 11-nor-9-carboxy-Δ9-tetrahydr ocannabinol (THCCOOH), morphine (MOP), codeine (COD), 6-monoacetylmorphine (6-MAM), and phencyclidine (PCP). The described GC-MS protocol is a practical and robust approach for routine forensic analysis of oral fluid. DSS offers a convenient and cost-effective sampling and extraction strategy, requiring only small sample volumes and allowing for simplified storage and transport. The analytical protocol provides high sensitivity and specificity for multiple analytes using minimal sample preparation. Its applicability in forensic toxicology makes it a useful tool for routine drug testing.

raw.abstractText:
Background

Ulcerative colitis is a relapsing inflammatory bowel disease driven by dysregulated immunity, epithelial barrier injury and microbial imbalance. Current therapies remain limited by relapse, adverse effects and incomplete response. Quercetin has anti-inflammatory and barrier-protective activities and ERK-MMP signaling may link inflammation to mucosal tissue damage.

Objectives

To evaluate whether the protective effects of quercetin in experimental ulcerative colitis (UC) are associated with modulation of ERK-MMP signaling, while avoiding causal overinterpretation beyond the animal and cellular evidence.

Methods

A dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced mouse model and a lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophage inflammatory model were used. Mice were allocated to the control, UC model and low-, medium- and high-dose quercetin groups. Disease activity index (DAI; unitless), colon length, histopathology, inflammatory cytokines and ERK/MMP-related molecules were evaluated by histological staining, ELISA, qRT-PCR and western blotting. In-vitro, quercetin was compared with the ERK phosphorylation inhibitor U0126 and an agonistic stimulus to explore pathway-related associations. The study was exploratory and did not include genetic rescue experiments or human validation.

Results

In DSS-treated mice, medium- and high-dose quercetin were associated with improved colon morphology, reduced DAI scores and partial restoration of colon length. Quercetin decreased pro-inflammatory cytokine expression and increased IL-10 expression. In both mouse colon tissues and LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 cells, quercetin was associated with reduced ERK1/2 activation and lower MMP-3 and MMP-9 expression, together with partial recovery of TIMP expression. These molecular changes were directionally consistent with the effects observed after ERK inhibition in-vitro.

Conclusion

Quercetin showed protective effects in experimental UC models and these effects may be associated with modulation of the ERK-MMP signaling axis. Further pathway-specific rescue experiments, pharmacokinetic studies and human-relevant models are required before this mechanism can be considered definitive or clinically translatable.

raw.abstractText: Wilson's disease (WD) is a genetic disorder caused by a mutation in the gene ATP7B. It results in the pathological deposition of copper mainly in the liver and the brain leading to hepatic and neurological manifestations. Medical management is effective in most patients (approximately 85%). It includes chelators (D-penicillamine and trientine), which are the mainstay of treatment, and zinc salts, which are used to inhibit the gastrointestinal absorption of copper. However, in cases of WD with neurological manifestations, patients take longer time to improve and sometimes have persistent clinical symptoms, and a few develop irreversible neurological damage despite adequate chelation. Generally, liver transplantation (LT) is indicated in acute fulminant hepatic failure or decompensated liver cirrhosis (despite adequate chelation). However, LT is still debatable for severe neurologic WD because of advanced or irreversible brain damage. There is a dearth of literature on the role of LT in neurological WD. This study aims to review the current literature concerning indications, contraindications, and outcomes of liver transplantation among children with neurological WD.

raw.abstractText: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental condition frequently associated with gastrointestinal (GI) disturbances and alterations in gut microbiota composition. Increasing evidence suggests that the microbiota-gut-brain axis may play a role in the pathophysiology of ASD, raising interest in microbiome-targeted therapies, including probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT). However, the clinical effectiveness and mechanisms of these interventions remain incompletely understood due to heterogeneous study designs and variable outcomes across trials. To systematically evaluate the clinical efficacy and mechanistic implications of psychobiotic interventions, including probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics, and FMT, in children with ASD. We conducted this systematic review in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. We also followed the methodological recommendations of the Cochrane Handbook. We searched different electronic databases, including PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, PsycINFO, CENTRAL, and CINAHL, from inception till February 2026. We included eligible randomized controlled trials, controlled clinical trials, cohort studies, and pre-post intervention studies evaluating psychobiotic therapies in children and adolescents (≤ 18 years) with ASD. The main outcomes were: (1) Changes in severity as assessed by a broad-spectrum measure of ASD symptomatology at the 3-month follow-up; and (2) Variation of core symptoms, based on validated behavioral scales, including the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule, the Childhood Autism Rating Scale (CARS), and the Social Responsiveness Scale (SRS). We measured the severity of GI symptoms, microbiome composition, biologicals, and safety as secondary outcomes. Risk of bias was determined with Risk of Bias tool version 2 and Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies of Interventions tools. Meta-analysis using random-effects models was conducted where appropriate. We reviewed 35 clinical studies that examined microbiome-targeted therapies in children with ASD. Overall, probiotics were associated with obvious improvements in GI symptoms and smaller, but noticeable, improvements in behavioral outcomes, although the benefits varied depending on the probiotic strains used, treatment duration, and whether children had GI problems at baseline. When data from selected probiotic studies were pooled, a moderate-to-large overall benefit was observed for GI symptom severity. Prebiotic supplementation mainly benefited gut function and microbial metabolic activity, with little and inconsistent impact on core autism symptoms. Synbiotic approaches-which combine probiotics with fermentable substrates-produced broader effects on the gut microbiome and were linked to modest improvements in both GI and behavioral symptoms. We observed that FMT showed the strongest overall effects among all microbiome-based interventions. Using quantitative analyses, we observed marked improvements in GI symptoms (GI SRS pooled SMD -2.71), along with a significant decrease in key behavioral measures, including social responsiveness (SRS pooled SMD -4.06), aberrant behavior (Aberrant Behavior Checklist -3.00), and overall autism severity (CARS -1.60). However, the strength of this evidence is tempered by the fact that many FMT studies were open-label or non-randomized, which limits confidence in the robustness of these findings. Across all microbiome-targeted therapies, benefits were most consistently observed for GI outcomes, whereas improvements in core ASD symptoms were more variable and less predictable. Microbiome-targeted therapies are a promising adjunctive strategy in managing children with ASD, especially for associated GI disorders. Probiotics and prebiotics provided the most reliable benefits for GI symptoms, while synbiotics may offer broader microbiome modulation, and FMT has the greatest observed improvements in both GI and behavioral outcomes. However, considerable heterogeneity across studies and limited high-quality randomized trials highlight the need for large, well-designed clinical trials with standardized intervention protocols to clarify clinical efficacy and guide future therapeutic recommendations.

raw.abstractText: Few direct-acting antiviral regimens are approved in China for children and adolescents with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection and data are limited on their efficacy and safety in this population. This retrospective, multi-centre study aimed to assess the real-world effectiveness and safety of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir (LDV/SOF) and sofosbuvir/velpatasvir (SOF/VEL) in Chinese paediatric patients. The study included patients aged 3-17 years from five hospitals across China who received either LDV/SOF or SOF/VEL for chronic HCV infection. The outcomes included the proportion of patients who achieved sustained virologic response at 12 weeks post-treatment (SVR12), normalisation rates of ALT and AST levels, and incidence of adverse events (AEs). A total of 129 patients from five sites were included and 128 completed 12 weeks of post-treatment follow-up. Mean age was 9.9 years (standard deviation, 3.9), with 30 (23.3%), 55 (42.6%), and 44 (34.1%) patients aged 3-6, 7-11, and 12-17 years, respectively, 84 (65.1%) were male, 62 (48.1%) were infected with genotype 3, and baseline ALT and AST levels were elevated in 64 (49.6%) and 75 (58.1%) patients, respectively. The SVR12 rate was 98.4% (126/128) in the overall population, remaining consistent across subgroups by sex, age, HCV genotype, or regimen. ALT and AST levels were normalised in all patients with available data. AEs were reported by 16.4% (21/128) of patients and none were serious. Collectively, this study demonstrated that LDV/SOF and SOF/VEL were highly effective and well tolerated in Chinese paediatric patients with chronic HCV infection.

raw.abstractText:
Background

Cannabis use may cause psychotic symptoms, such as hallucinations and delusions, as well as persistent amotivation with reduced motivation, inactivity, and cognitive impairment. Although described as cannabis-related amotivational syndrome, it is not recognized as an independent diagnostic entity and overlaps clinically with the negative symptoms of schizophrenia and mood disorders. We report a case of persistent amotivation following cannabis-related psychosis that improved after electroconvulsive therapy (ECT).

Case

A 19-year-old man developed auditory hallucinations, persecutory delusions, and agitation associated with cannabis use and was admitted to a psychiatric hospital. Antipsychotic treatment improved the psychotic symptoms, but marked amotivation and inactivity, accompanied by low performance on cognitive screening, and significantly impaired daily functioning. Depressed mood and appetite loss were not evident. Although negative symptoms of schizophrenia remained a differential diagnosis, the presentation was consistent with cannabis-related amotivational syndrome. Amantadine produced limited improvement. Following ECT, the Apathy Scale score improved from 24 to 7 and the Mini-Mental State Examination score increased from 19 to 26, with improvements in motivation, activity, and daily functioning.

Discussion

This case demonstrates that clinically significant amotivation may persist after cannabis-related psychotic symptoms improve. Persistently reduced motivation and inactivity should not be assumed to represent primary negative symptoms of schizophrenia; rather, clinicians should carefully consider mood symptoms and cannabis-related amotivation in the differential diagnosis. This case also suggests that ECT may represent a treatment option for severe, persistent amotivation following cannabis-related psychosis. However, because this was a single case, further validation through additional cases and long-term follow-up is required.

raw.abstractText: The therapeutic effects of antipsychotic drugs are primarily achieved through dopamine D2 receptor antagonism. However, excessive striatal D2 receptor blockade is associated with extrapyramidal side effects (EPS) in schizophrenic patients. Clinical studies indicate a therapeutic window of approximately 60%-80% striatal D2 receptor occupancy, with higher occupancy increasing the risk of EPS. However, conventional rodent dosing paradigms rarely maintain clinically comparable receptor occupancy, limiting their translational relevance. Here, we investigated whether continuous antipsychotic administration designed to achieve clinically relevant striatal D2 receptor occupancy can be used to evaluate extrapyramidal motor liability in mice. Using an occupancy-guided dosing paradigm, we continuously administered haloperidol or olanzapine and assessed catalepsy as an index of EPS. To validate catalepsy as an EPS-like phenotype, we examined whether it could be attenuated by an anticholinergic agent, consistent with the clinical management of EPS. Catalepsy was observed only under high-occupancy haloperidol condition. A significant increase in catalepsy time was observed only in mice receiving haloperidol at a dose producing approximately 90% D2 receptor occupancy on day 3, whereas no catalepsy was detected under lower occupancy conditions with either haloperidol or olanzapine. Importantly, haloperidol-induced catalepsy was significantly attenuated by scopolamine. Together, these findings demonstrate that an occupancy-guided continuous antipsychotic dosing paradigm enables evaluation of EPS-like behavior under clinically relevant D2 receptor occupancy conditions in mice, providing a translational framework linking clinical PET studies with preclinical research.

raw.abstractText: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterised by persistent airway injury and remodelling, and the mechanisms by which Chai-Hu-Gui-Zhi Decoction (CGD) acts in COPD remain unclear. This study investigated whether CGD attenuates airway remodelling through the TGF-β1/Smads-EMT-ECM signalling axis. A mouse COPD model was established by cigarette-smoke exposure plus intranasal lipopolysaccharide. After model induction, mice received dexamethasone acetate or low-, medium- or high-dose CGD for 28 days. UHPLC-MS/MS, network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics, proteomics, metabolomics, ELISA, western blotting, RT-PCR, pulmonary function testing and histopathology were integrated. CGD dose-dependently improved pulmonary function and lung pathology and reduced BALF total protein, NO, VEGF, IFN-γ, MPO, CXCL1 and serum 8-OHdG. Multi-omics and network analyses implicated phenylalanine/tyrosine/tryptophan biosynthesis, the histidine-glutamate-hypoxanthine axis, MAPK, PI3K-Akt and TGF-β1-related pathways. Validation showed that CGD decreased TGF-β1, p-SMAD2/3, SMAD2/3, MMP-9 and TIMP-1; increased SMAD7 and E-cadherin; and regulated Smad2/Smad3/Smad7 mRNA. CGD may attenuate COPD airway remodelling, in association with suppressed TGF-β1/Smads signalling, restored SMAD7-mediated feedback, limited EMT and rebalanced ECM remodelling.

raw.abstractText:
Background

Breast cancer (BC) remains a significant global health threat with complex pathogenesis often linked to chemotherapy resistance and inflammatory microenvironments. Histidine triad nucleotide-binding protein 2 (HINT2) is a mitochondrial protein involved in metabolism and immunity, but its specific role in BC and potential as a therapeutic target require further elucidation.

Objectives

This study aimed to identify novel therapeutic targets for BC and evaluate the anti-tumor efficacy and molecular mechanisms of Albiflorin (Al), a natural monoterpene glycoside.

Methods

Proteomic profiling was performed on BC xenografts in nude mice to identify differentially expressed proteins. In-vivo and in-vitro models (MDA-MB-231 cells) were established to assess the effects of Al (20 mg/kg or 20 µM) on tumor growth, apoptosis and cytokine production. Molecular docking and co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) were used to investigate the interactions among HINT2, NLRP3 and Al.

Results

HINT2 was significantly upregulated in BC tissues and identified as a primary pro-tumorigenic factor. Co-IP confirmed an endogenous interaction between HINT2 and NLRP3. Al exhibited strong binding affinity to HINT2 (-7.36 kcal/mol) and significantly suppressed tumor volume and weight. Furthermore, Al treatment downregulated the HINT2/NLRP3 axis, reduced inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α) and promoted apoptosis by modulating Caspase-3, Bax and Bcl-2 levels.

Conclusion

Albiflorin suppresses BC progression by inhibiting the HINT2/NLRP3 signaling pathway, suggesting HINT2 is a viable biomarker and Al a promising therapeutic agent for BC treatment.

Background and aims

Liver disease is a significant risk for people who inject drugs due to the high burden of hepatitis C virus (HCV). There is limited data on the impact of the direct-acting antiviral (DAA) therapy era on liver disease among people who inject drugs. This study evaluated baseline and longitudinal liver disease in a national cohort of people who inject drugs recruited over three Waves: 2018-2019, 2019-2021, and 2023-2025.

Methods

The ETHOS Engage Study is an observational cohort of people who inject drugs attending drug treatment clinics and needle and syringe programs in Australia. Participants completed a questionnaire and underwent point-of-care HCV RNA testing (Xpert HCV Viral Load Fingerstick) and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) by vibration-controlled transient hepatic elastography (FibroScan). Advanced chronic liver disease was defined by LSM of 10 kPa or above.

Results

Among all enrolments with a valid LSM (n = 3126, 79% recruited at drug treatment clinics), 11% had advanced chronic liver disease, decreasing from 12.0% (154/1287) in 2018-2019 to 7.9% (66/839) in 2019-2021, and 6.4% (62/967) in 2023-2025. In adjusted analyses, participants recruited between 2019-2021 and 2023-2025 were less likely to have advanced chronic liver disease (vs. 2018-2019; aOR 0.66, 95% CI: 0.48-0.90 and aOR 0.56, 95% CI: 0.40-0.77, respectively). Current HCV infection declined from 24% in 2018-2019 to 10% in 2023-2025. Among participants with LSM in more than one wave and current HCV infection at first visit and no current HCV infection at second visit (n = 44), advanced chronic liver disease declined from 19% to 5%.

Conclusions

Unrestricted access to DAA therapies in Australia has been associated with reduced liver disease burden among people who inject drugs. Monitoring of liver health in this population is important, given potential ageing and non-HCV liver disease impacts.

raw.abstractText: Excessive alcohol consumption is a significant global health concern, causing over 200 adverse health outcomes, including liver disease, cardiovascular disease, neuropsychiatric disorders, and malignancies. Among these, alcohol-related liver disease (ALD) stands out as a leading contributor to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) worldwide. Moreover, alcohol accounts for 27% of deaths from cirrhosis and chronic liver disease, with 30% of HCC-related mortality attributed to alcohol use. Despite its severity, abstinence from alcohol markedly improves survival, even in advanced stages of ALD, highlighting the centrality of cessation efforts in disease management. HCC represents a major global health challenge, especially in individuals with ALD. Unfortunately, HCC often presents at an advanced stage, limiting treatment efficacy and resulting in a dismal 5-year survival rate of 3.3%. Beyond HCC, alcohol use is linked to an elevated risk of other malignancies, such as cancers of the oral cavity, pharynx, larynx, oesophagus (squamous cell), liver (hepatocellular), colorectum, and female breast; compounding the disease burden. This review explores the intricate relationship between alcohol exposure, primary liver cancer, and other alcohol-related malignancies. It highlights the pathophysiological mechanisms, epidemiological trends, and the importance of alcohol abstinence in mitigating disease progression. Future research must focus on innovative approaches to improve prevention, surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment in this high-risk population.

Aim

To analyse the use of opioids in children with cancer and the experiences of their family members regarding opioids used in pain management to improve family nursing.

Design

An integrative review.

Methods

A systematic literature search was carried out in four databases (CINAHL, MEDLINE, PsycInfo and Scopus) in August 2023, and was subsequently updated to include studies up to the end of 2024. Sixteen peer-reviewed research articles met the inclusion criteria and were included in a quality appraisal and analysis.

Results

Of the wide range of opioids used to treat pain in children with cancer, morphine and fentanyl stood out as the most used. The prevalent routes of opioid administration was intravenous and enteral. Limited research has been conducted on the experiences of family members of children with cancer in the context of opioids used for pain management. Furthermore, there is a scarcity of studies that describe the experiences of siblings from the same perspective. Parental experiences were particularly described as concerns about and a desire to refuse opioid use, although satisfaction with opioid use was also described.

Conclusions

Opioids are particularly significant in managing pain among children with cancer. Therefore, the use of opioids in this patient group should be comprehensively studied, and healthcare professionals should receive sufficient training. The experiences of parents conclude that they require sufficient information and guidance on the management of their children's severe pain and the analgesics used to treat it. The notable lack of research regarding the experiences of siblings in connection with the use of opioids for the management of a child's pain addresses the need for further research from these perspectives. More research on experiences during the different phases of cancer treatment is needed. Further research employing qualitative methods will be essential for enhancing family nursing.

Background

Exposure to mercury (Hg) is well-established to induce menstrual cycle disorders and disrupt sex hormone functions. Astragalus species, characterized by their potent antioxidant and anti-apoptotic properties, have shown potential in mitigating these adverse effects by promoting folliculogenesis and restoring hormonal balance.

Objectives

This study aimed to evaluate the protective effects of Astragalus microcephalus polysaccharides (APS), both alone and in combination with vitamin E and selenium (Vit E+Se), against ovarian damage and oxidative stress induced by mercuric chloride toxicity in rats.

Methods

Thirty-six female Wistar rats were synchronized via vaginal smear and randomly assigned to six groups: Control, Mercury (0.43 mg/kg HgCl2), APS (2.7 g/kg), Vit E+Se, Mercury+APS and Mercury+Vit E+Se. Following a 15-day subacute exposure period, serum levels of estradiol, LH and FSH were measured. Oxidative stress markers and ovarian histopathology were evaluated. Apoptotic and inflammatory pathways were assessed through immunohistochemical staining of Caspase-3, AIF and NF-κB.

Results

Hg-induced reductions in hormone levels were significantly restored to near control levels in the APS-treated groups and antioxidant levels were notably elevated in these groups, indicating mitigation of oxidative stress. Furthermore, immunohistochemical analysis revealed a significant reduction in stromal and follicular degeneration and a decrease in apoptotic activity in the ovaries of rats treated with APS.

Conclusion

APS exerts a significant protective effect against mercury-induced ovarian toxicity. This protection is mediated through the attenuation of oxidative stress, inflammation and apoptosis, as evidenced by the modulation of Caspase-3, AIF and NF-κB pathways. The results suggest that APS, particularly in synergy with vitamin E and selenium, offers a potential therapeutic strategy for managing heavy metal-induced reproductive damage.

raw.abstractText: Recreational nitrous oxide (N2O) use has risen in recent years and is increasingly accessible in high-volume cartridges and canisters. N2O oxidizes cobalamin and functionally inhibits methionine synthase disrupting methylation pathways essential for myelin maintenance and DNA metabolism. Serum vitamin B12 levels may be normal despite functional deficiency, making markers such as homocysteine and methylmalonic acid helpful to confirm the diagnosis. Clinical manifestations range from peripheral neuropathy and megaloblastic anemia to subacute combined degeneration (SCD), a demyelinating myelopathy classically involving the dorsal columns (and sometimes corticospinal tracts). Early recognition and prompt parenteral vitamin B12 replacement may reduce the risk of irreversible deficits.

raw.abstractText:
Background

Bacterial vaginosis (BV) is a common vaginal infection in women of reproductive age and is often linked to a vaginal microbiota imbalance. Conventional antibiotics such as metronidazole are effective but are associated with side effects and recurrence, prompting interest in herbal alternatives.

Objectives

To compare the clinical efficacy of medicinal plants versus metronidazole in the treatment of bacterial vaginosis using evidence from randomized clinical trials.

Methods

This narrative review examined randomized clinical trials evaluating herbal interventions for bacterial vaginosis. Web of Science, Scopus, PubMed, and ScienceDirect were searched for studies published up to March 2026. The included studies assessed herbal interventions administered orally or vaginally, alone or with conventional metronidazole therapy. Information on plant species, study design, participants, diagnostic criteria, interventions, results, and conclusions was extracted and synthesized narratively.

Results

Twenty-four published articles were included, covering a range of medicinal plants, including Allium sativum, Myrtus communis, Quercus species, Berberis vulgaris, Zataria multiflora, Calendula officinalis, Cymbopogon olivieri, and others. Herbal therapies showed efficacy comparable to or superior to metronidazole, with fewer side effects and lower recurrence rates. Their effects are attributed to bioactive compounds, including allicin, curcumin, berberine, tannins, flavonoids, and essential oils, which exhibit antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant properties.

Conclusions

Medicinal plants appear to be safe and effective alternatives or adjuncts for bacterial vaginosis; however, the heterogeneity in study designs and short follow-up periods limits definitive conclusions. Further well-designed, multicenter randomized trials with standardized protocols and long-term follow-up, along with studies exploring individual plants and their mechanisms of action, are needed to confirm efficacy, safety, and reproducibility and to support evidence-based use.

Background

Caffeine is consumed for its presumed cognitive benefits, yet controlled studies have repeatedly failed to find effects on inhibitory control. Cross-sectional work suggests that people with elevated attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms may benefit from chronic, moderate caffeine consumption, but whether acute intake improves cognition in proportion to symptom severity has not been tested experimentally.

Aims

We tested whether 250 mg of caffeine improves active inhibition (withholding a prepared response) and reactive inhibition (resolving response conflict), and whether ADHD symptom severity moderates these effects.

Methods

In a preregistered, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial, a nonclinical sample of 36 young adults received 250 mg of caffeine or placebo in counterbalanced order, with testing 45 min after ingestion. Active inhibition was assessed with a Go/No-Go task (204 trials), reactive inhibition with an arrow flanker task (200 trials) and symptoms with the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale. Mixed-effects models included treatment, symptom severity, their interaction and ten covariates; Bayes factors quantified evidence for the null.

Results

Both tasks produced their benchmark effects (dz = 1.24 and 1.09) and all indices were reliable (split-half r = 0.73-0.98). Caffeine affected neither commission errors (BF01 = 4.98), response criterion (5.14), Go reaction time (2.83), reaction time variability (4.35), flanker reaction time (5.49) nor flanker accuracy (5.09). ADHD symptoms moderated no effect (15 preregistered tests; smallest p = 0.514), yet predicted performance itself (flanker accuracy r = -0.42), indicating that the null is not due to an insensitive measure.

Conclusions

Caffeine produced no acute benefit for either form of inhibition, and ADHD symptoms did not moderate its effects. Bayes factors supported the absence rather than the nondetection of these effects, arguing against an acute improvement of inhibitory control that scales with ADHD symptom severity in nonclinical young adults. Whether this also holds for chronic consumption or for adults with diagnosed ADHD remains to be tested.

Objective

Caffeine could improve cognitive functions, but study protocols usually prohibit drinking coffee before cognitive testing. However, regular coffee consumers may experience withdrawal effects when they cannot drink their habitual coffee, which may impair cognitive performance. Therefore, we tested the effects of overnight coffee abstinence in regular coffee consumers: once allowing to drink their coffee and once not drinking coffee. The cognitive performance was compared with non-regular coffee consumers.

Methods

Thirty regular coffee consumers (RCCs) and 25 non-regular consumers (N-RCCs) took part in this study. RCCs were tested after their habitual morning coffee (c-RCC) and after overnight abstinence (a-RCC); N-RCCs were tested once. A cognitive battery assessed reaction time (RT), processing speed (digit symbol substitution test), working memory, verbal learning/memory and executive function (Stroop). Sleep quality was included as a covariate.

Results

Compared to c-RCC, overnight coffee abstinence significantly slowed RTs but did not affect the performance in the other cognitive tasks. In the a-RCC condition, but not the c-RCC condition, the RTs were slower than those of the N-RCCs, while accuracy measures were comparable across groups. Sleep quality did not alter these findings.

Conclusions

Overnight coffee abstinence selectively slowed RT, and no statistical support was found for effects on memory or executive function. This suggests that overnight coffee abstinence protocols may introduce withdrawal-related RT slowing as a confound in habitual consumers, whereas other cognitive domains may not be affected. Allowing habitual consumers to maintain normal coffee intake could reduce this bias, supporting tailored rather than uniform abstinence requirements based on the specific outcomes studied.

Purpose

Insomnia is a prevalent neurological disorder often caused by stress, anxiety, and imbalances in the GABAergic system. Although benzodiazepines like diazepam (DZP) are commonly prescribed, their long-term use is associated with adverse effects, including dependence and impaired coordination. Therefore, there is growing interest in natural alternatives with safer pharmacological profiles.

Method

This study aimed to investigate the sedative-like potential of L (+)-tartaric acid (LTA), a naturally occurring organic acid, through both in vivo and in silico approaches targeting the γ-aminobutyric acid A (GABAA) receptor. Sedative-like activity was evaluated in Swiss albino mice using thiopental sodium-induced sleeping time, open-field, and rotarod tests.

Findings

LTA significantly reduced sleep latency and prolonged sleep duration in a dose-dependent manner, with the higher dose (240 mg/kg) producing a more pronounced effect. Co-administration of LTA with DZP further enhanced thiopental-induced hypnosis. In the open-field test, LTA reduced locomotor and exploratory activities, as evidenced by decreases in square crossings, rearing, and grooming behaviors. Rotarod assessment demonstrated a dose-dependent reduction in motor coordination and neuromuscular performance, although the impairment remained less pronounced than that produced by DZP at the lower tested dose. Molecular docking revealed lower binding affinity than DZP but demonstrated multiple hydrogen-bond (HB) interactions with key amino acid (AA) residues of the GABAA receptor, suggesting a potentially stable receptor interaction.

Conclusion

Collectively, the behavioral and computational findings indicate that LTA possesses sedative-like properties and may modulate GABAergic neurotransmission. Further mechanistic, pharmacokinetic, and electrophysiological studies are required to clarify its precise mode of action and therapeutic potential.

Both compounds were characterised by multinuclear NMR, IR, MS and elemental analysis; their purity was established by reverse-phase HPLC (98.8% for 1 and > 99% for 2 after recrystallisation), and their structures were determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Crystal structure and Hirshfeld surface analyses reveal a tautomerism-controlled switch in supramolecular assembly: compound 1 adopts an enol-imine form, generating discrete amide-phenol dimers via a robust heterosynthon, while 2 exists as a keto-enamine, forming infinite N-H···O hydrogen-bonded chains reinforced by π-π stacking of naphthalene rings. DFT calculations (B3LYP/6-311 + G(d,p)) support these findings, showing distinct charge distributions and a reduced HOMO-LUMO gap for 2, consistent with enhanced electronic polarizability. Molecular docking against acetylcholinesterase (PDB: 1EVE) predicted that both compounds adopt binding modes within the catalytic gorge, with 2 showing particularly favourable interactions within the catalytic gorge. These predictions were tested experimentally. In a colorimetric AChE inhibitor screening assay both compounds inhibit the enzyme in a concentration-dependent manner, with IC<sub>50</sub> values of 22.5 µM (1) and 55.0 µM (2) against 15.0 µM for the galantamine reference measured alongside. Computational ADME/Tox profiling tentatively predicts compliance with Lipinski and Veber criteria, oral bioavailability, blood-brain barrier permeation, and acceptable toxicity classes, pending experimental confirmation. raw.abstractText: The collagen triple helix is the most abundant protein structural motif in animals. It tolerates any amino acid in its Xaa and Yaa positions but demands glycine (Gly) at every third position, where the residue packs into the sterically forbidding core of the triple helix and donates the recurring interstrand N-H⋯OC hydrogen bond that stitches the three strands together. (2S)-Proline (Pro) and (2S,4R)-4-hydroxyproline (Hyp) are enriched far above their proteome-wide abundance because they preorganize individual strands into the polyproline II conformation, lowering the entropic cost of folding. We asked whether the triple helix is intrinsically stable enough to form from strands that carry no such preorganization, that is, from polyglycine. To offset the conformational entropy of a Gly-rich tract, we embedded Gly<sub>6</sub> within flanking triple-helical (Pro-Hyp-Gly)<sub>n</sub> clamps in Ac-(Pro-Hyp-Gly)<sub>6</sub>-Gly<sub>6</sub>-(Pro-Hyp-Gly)<sub>5</sub>-Pro-Hyp-NH<sub>2</sub> and compared it with an otherwise identical peptide in which Gly<sub>6</sub> was replaced by two [2-(2-aminoethoxy)ethoxy]acetic acid units, a flexible, length-matched spacer that lacks most of the regularly spaced backbone amides of Gly<sub>6</sub>. Circular dichroism spectroscopy revealed the diagnostic positive band at 225 nm. The molar ellipticity of the spacer-containing control was 86% of that of the Gly<sub>6</sub>-containing peptide, matching the 35/41 = 85% ratio of residues capable of triple-helix formation and consistent with the Gly<sub>6</sub> segment contributing to the triple-helical signal. Thermal denaturation yielded a T<sub>m</sub> of 46.8°C for the Gly<sub>6</sub>-containing peptide, 6.3°C higher than that of the matched spacer control. This added stability indicates that the polyglycine tract is not merely accommodated within the helix but contributes stabilizing interstrand hydrogen bonds. Together, these data indicate that three polyglycine strands can form a collagen triple helix when flanked by triple-helical clamps. This result is consistent with the idea that the triple-helical architecture predates the recruitment of Pro and Hyp, informs the evolutionary origin of collagen, and offers a blunt-ended, symmetric scaffold for designing peptidic triple helices.

raw.abstractText: Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) is a prevalent metabolic disorder affecting approximately 14% of pregnancies worldwide, with increasing incidence linked to rising obesity rates among women of reproductive age. GDM significantly impacts placental structure and function, leading to adverse maternal and fetal outcomes. Inositols, particularly myo-inositol (myo-Ins), play important roles in cellular signaling, glucose homeostasis, and insulin sensitivity, making them relevant to GDM pathophysiology. Myo-Ins, the most abundant inositol stereoisomer, is obtained through dietary intake and biosynthesis, with its metabolism intricately linked to insulin signaling. This review explores the role of myo-Ins in placental metabolism and its potential implications for GDM management. We discuss the potential mechanisms by which myo-Ins might influence glucose homeostasis, oxidative stress, inflammation, and lipid metabolism in the placenta, highlighting potential protective effects against GDM-induced placental dysfunction. Some clinical evidence suggests that myo-Ins supplementation may reduce the risk of GDM, improve insulin sensitivity, and mitigate adverse pregnancy outcomes. However, the timing, dosage, and specific placental effects require further investigation to optimize therapeutic efficacy. This review underscores the potential of myo-Ins as an adjunctive therapy for GDM, emphasizing the need for further research to elucidate mechanisms of action and long-term benefits for maternal and fetal health.

While insulin activates the sympathetic nervous system in experimental settings, whether therapeutic insulin administration is associated with cardiac sympathetic predominance under free-living conditions remains unclear. This prospective observational study investigated the association between insulin dosing and cardiac autonomic balance in adults with type 1 diabetes managed exclusively with insulin therapy. Participants underwent continuous heart rate variability (HRV) and glucose monitoring over 4 consecutive days during routine daily activities. Cardiac sympathetic predominance was assessed using the low-frequency power to high-frequency power (LF/HF) ratio derived from HRV analysis, and associations were evaluated using generalized estimating equations. A higher last bolus insulin dose was associated with an increased LF/HF ratio during the early sleep phase. A higher basal insulin dose was also associated with an increased LF/HF ratio during the late sleep phase. These associations persisted after adjustment for mean glucose and mean absolute glucose change during the corresponding sleep phases. Under free-living conditions, higher insulin doses were associated with dose-dependent increases in cardiac sympathetic predominance, independent of glycemic profiles. These findings suggest that insulin dosing may be linked to cardiac autonomic regulation in individuals with type 1 diabetes, highlighting the importance of considering cardiac autonomic balance and potential cardiovascular risk when optimizing insulin therapy.

Article highlights

The relationship between therapeutic insulin administration and cardiac autonomic balance under free-living conditions remains unclear. We examined whether insulin dosing was associated with cardiac sympathetic predominance during daily life in adults with type 1 diabetes managed with insulin therapy. Higher last bolus and basal insulin doses were associated with increased cardiac sympathetic predominance during the early and late sleep phases, respectively, independent of glycemic profiles. These findings suggest that insulin dosing patterns may be linked to cardiac autonomic balance, with potential implications for optimizing insulin therapy in type 1 diabetes.

Background

Prolonged exposure to hepatotoxic antiretroviral therapy (ART) could lead to chronic liver injury, which might increase risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). We used causal inference methods to evaluate if cumulative exposure to ART with known mechanisms of chronic liver injury is associated with HCC among people with HIV (PWH), by chronic liver disease (CLD) status.

Methods

We conducted a cohort study of antiretroviral-naive PWH with and without diagnosed CLD who initiated ART in the Veterans Affairs between 1999 and 2023. Exposure to ART with known mechanism of chronic liver injury (mitochondrial toxicity or accumulation of toxic intermediates) was determined monthly through prescription fills. Incident HCC was identified by Veterans Affairs National Cancer Registry and/or recorded diagnoses. Marginal structural models estimated odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) of HCC associated with cumulative exposure to chronic liver injury-inducing ART compared with ART without chronic liver injury mechanisms, by CLD status.

Results

Among 11,854 PWH without CLD and 6771 PWH with CLD, we observed 112 and 378 HCC events, respectively. Among PWH without CLD, ≥4 years of exposure to chronic liver injury-inducing ART was associated with HCC when compared with ≥4 years of use of ART without chronic liver injury mechanisms (OR = 4.02 [95% CI: 1.00-16.24]). Among PWH with CLD, ≥4 years of exposure to chronic liver injury-inducing ART was not associated with HCC (OR = 1.36; 95% CI: 0.68-2.72).

Conclusion

Four or more years of ART with a chronic liver injury mechanism was associated with HCC among PWH without CLD, but not those with CLD.

raw.abstractText: Melatonin is best known as a pineal hormone that regulates circadian rhythms, but the skin also possesses an intrinsic melatoninergic system capable of local synthesis, metabolism and signalling. This system encompasses classical melatonin receptors, biologically active metabolites, non-classical signalling pathways and receptor-independent intracellular actions involved in cutaneous stress responses, with emerging evidence for broader roles in skin homeostasis. In this review, we integrate current mechanistic and clinical evidence on the cutaneous melatoninergic system and critically examine its therapeutic relevance. Human evidence is most consistent for the photoprotective effects of topical melatonin, whereas clinical data for photoaging, radiation dermatitis, wound healing, hair disorders, inflammatory dermatoses, pigmentary disorders and chronic pruritus remain limited or preliminary. Interpretation is further constrained by small sample sizes, heterogeneous formulations, short follow-up and frequent use of combination products. Importantly, the clinical efficacy of exogenous melatonin and evidence that the endogenous cutaneous melatoninergic system represents a disease-modifying therapeutic target are distinct questions. Establishing the therapeutic relevance of the endogenous system will require characterisation of disease-associated alterations in local melatonin synthesis, metabolism and signalling, demonstration of molecular target engagement, and linkage to clinically meaningful outcomes.

raw.abstractText: Melatonin (MEL) is an endogenous hormone that regulates circadian rhythm, immune function and oxidative stress responses. Norepinephrine (NE), an endogenous catecholamine, increases blood pressure through the sympathetic nervous system and is commonly administered intraoperatively or in the clinically ill patient for hemodynamic support. Although endogenous NE is known to stimulate MEL synthesis, the effects of exogenous intravenous NE on plasma MEL concentration, particularly under general anaesthesia (GA), remain poorly characterised. This study examined the influence of intravenous NE on plasma MEL concentrations in healthy volunteers, both awake and under general anaesthesia. A secondary analysis was conducted using data from a prospective, single-centre, cross-over study involving volunteers who received stepwise NE infusions while awake and under total intravenous general anaesthesia. Arterial blood samples were collected to determine plasma MEL and NE concentrations. Linear mixed-effects modelling was used to assess the relationship between NE and MEL concentrations. A total of 36 healthy volunteers were enroled, yielding 417 MEL-NE samples. Intravenous NE administration was significantly associated with higher plasma MEL concentration, corresponding to an estimated 26% increase in MEL per 1 standard-deviation increase in NE concentration (Estimate = 0.230, p < 0.001). MEL concentrations were approximately 43% higher in the awake phase compared to GA (Estimate = 0.356, p < 0.001). GA did not significantly modify the NE-MEL association (Estimate = -0.02877, p = 0.528). Substantial positive correlation was observed between baseline MEL concentrations and the magnitude of the response to NE administration (r = 0.74). In conclusion, intravenous NE increases plasma MEL concentrations in both awake and anaesthetised individuals. Substantial interindividual variation in MEL response suggests underlying physiological differences. Future studies should explore the long-term effects of NE administration on MEL concentrations. raw.abstractText:
Background

Sleep deprivation and poor sleep quality are critical problems among intensive care unit (ICU) patients, with significant implications for recovery, delirium onset and clinical outcomes. Despite growing scientific interest, no bibliometric study has systematically mapped the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of this field.

Aim

To analyse the bibliometric characteristics and thematic structure of publications on sleep deprivation, sleep promotion and sleep quality in ICU patients indexed in the Web of Science (WoS) database between 1983 and 2026.

Study design

A descriptive and evaluative bibliometric analysis was conducted. Data were retrieved on April 26, 2026, from the WoS Core Collection using a comprehensive search strategy. Publications were filtered by document type, WoS categories (nursing, critical care medicine, anaesthesiology) and index (SCI-EXPANDED, SSCI, ESCI). Data were analysed using R software with the Biblioshiny interface, and annual publication trends were evaluated using Microsoft Excel.

Results

Of 11 418 publications retrieved, 379 met the inclusion criteria, spanning 37 years (1983-2026). Linear regression revealed a statistically significant positive trend in publication output (β = 0.643, R2 = 0.704, r = 0.839, p < 0.001), with mean annual publications of 10.24 ± 8.83 and notable acceleration from the 2000s onwards. Thematic mapping identified 'sleep', 'sleep deprivation' and 'delirium' as motor themes both highly central and well developed. Emerging concepts included circadian rhythm, actigraphy, fatigue, pain and anxiety.

Conclusions

ICU sleep research has grown substantially over four decades, with sleep deprivation and delirium emerging as co-dominant research priorities. Thematic gaps and emerging clusters identified in this analysis highlight important directions for future nursing research and evidence-based practice development in critical care.

Relevance to clinical practice

This bibliometric analysis identified sleep deprivation and delirium as the co-dominant motor themes of ICU sleep research, and intervention-related concepts such as earplugs, eye masks and melatonin as emerging clusters. These evidence-based trends can guide ICU nurses in prioritizing targeted sleep promotion protocols and support policymakers in directing resources toward the most scientifically mature intervention areas in critical care.

raw.abstractText: We investigated the effects of angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs) on the progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD). This retrospective cohort study used data from the Korean nationwide claims data to identify patients with AD aged 60-79 years in 2010. ARB users and nonusers were 1:1 propensity score matched. Cox proportional hazards regression evaluated AD progression, defined as memantine initiation and mortality. Active-comparator and dose-response analyses were conducted. ARB use was associated with lower risks of memantine initiation (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.79; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.70-0.89) and mortality (HR = 0.83; 95% CI = 0.76-0.89). Cumulative exposure analyses showed stronger associations in the highest exposure categories, including 2-3 years of ARB use and ≥ 2 DDD-years, whereas associations in the lower exposure categories were not statistically significant. In active-comparator analyses, ARBs were associated with lower mortality risk than ACE inhibitors and beta-blockers, but not with dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (CCBs). ARB use may be a reasonable antihypertensive choice in patients with AD, although the comparable outcomes between ARBs and CCBs suggest that these associations may not be unique to ARBs and may instead reflect shared blood pressure-lowering and vascular effects. Further prospective research is warranted to optimize antihypertensive selection in patients with AD.
